question_text: A 12-month-old child passed away after suffering from craniofacial abnormalities, neurologic dysfunction, and hepatomegaly. Analysis of the child’s blood plasma shows an increase in very long chain fatty acids. The cellular analysis demonstrates dysfunction of an organelle responsible for the breakdown of these fatty acids within the cell. Postmortem, the child is diagnosed with Zellweger syndrome. The family is informed about the autosomal recessive inheritance pattern of the disease and their carrier status. Which of the following processes is deficient in the dysfunctional organelle in this disease?

                    ### Question
                    A 12-month-old child passed away after suffering from craniofacial abnormalities, neurologic dysfunction, and hepatomegaly. Analysis of the child’s blood plasma shows an increase in very long chain fatty acids. The cellular analysis demonstrates dysfunction of an organelle responsible for the breakdown of these fatty acids within the cell. Postmortem, the child is diagnosed with Zellweger syndrome. The family is informed about the autosomal recessive inheritance pattern of the disease and their carrier status. Which of the following processes is deficient in the dysfunctional organelle in this disease?

This is supported by the chain linking dysfunction of the organelle to fatty acid breakdown deficiency, which aligns with the standard consensus on the disease. The evidence path showing fatty acids in blood plasma linked to the dysfunction of the organelle further supports this conclusion.
